Dota 2 is a great MOBA that's being held back by nothing more than its player base and mediocre management.

Before you're allowed to play ranked, you're forced to endure 100 hours of unranked matchmaking. Doesn't sound too bad in theory, until you realize that unranked is essentially a free-for-all with absolutely no standards.

You'll be matched with players who can barely manage to breathe without choking on their own saliva, as well as players with over 7,000 games under their belts. You'll encounter smurfs and players who don't care about winning. Not necessarily because they don't want to win, but because they refuse to learn, hiding behind the classic excuse: "It's unranked, bro."

While unranked isn't something you're supposed to take particularly seriously, when you're still grinding through those 100 hours, you don't really have a choice. You're effectively being held hostage by people who have absolutely no respect for your time.

Furthermore, there isn't a single good region to play in, as each one comes with its own unique brand of toxicity.

Play on EU East, and you'll be greeted by four egotistical morons suffering from main character syndrome, who refuse to play support and wouldn't buy a ward to save their lives.

Play on EU West, and you'll be met with four misfits who refuse to communicate in English.

Play on NA, whether East or West, and there's a 50% chance your match will contain bots. And no, I'm not talking about Valve's bots. I'm talking about mediocre, third-rate scripts that run down lanes and die repeatedly.

"Are you sure they're not just new, bad players?"

Yes, I am. Every single one of these bots follows the same naming conventions and behavioral patterns: "AdjectiveName####", usually accompanied by a QR code or a picture of a girl as their profile picture. They also constantly spam chat wheel emotes, making them about as subtle as a brick through a window.

And the saddest part of all this is that the game itself is genuinely fantastic.

When you find yourself in a match with nine other like-minded individuals who have even a shred of competitive spirit and genuinely want to win, there's no other game that comes close to the satisfaction of winning an intense, hour-long match of Dota.

The hero design is amazing, the mechanics are smooth and satisfying, and the items are meaningful, often fundamentally changing how you approach and play the game. There's an incredible amount of depth here, and very few games can deliver the same experience.

People often say that Valve doesn't care. Personally, I think Valve is ashamed of its own creation and, more importantly, the community it has cultivated.

I would pay every cent I have, and every cent I will ever earn, just to gather the entire player base into one gigantic trebuchet and launch them into shark-infested waters.

Welcome to the Never-Ending Game.

Dota 2 is a strange place.

You enter looking for entertainment, spend hundreds of hours trying to understand it, thousands more trying to master it, and eventually realize that you might never truly understand it.

It's a game where five strangers are expected to work together like a perfectly coordinated team, where one tiny mistake can destroy a 60-minute match, and where the difference between an absolute genius and a complete fool is sometimes just one decision.

Every hero has a story. Every item has a purpose. Every match has its own chaos.

You can experience the most incredible comeback of your life, followed immediately by a defeat so ridiculous that you start questioning your existence.

There are beautiful moments hidden between all the madness. A perfectly executed team fight, a game-winning Black Hole, an unexpected Rampage, or that one teammate who actually knows what they're doing.

And then there is the other side of Dota 2...

The toxicity, the endless arguments, the questionable decisions, the matchmaking, and the occasional feeling that the entire universe is personally against you.

Yet, somehow, you keep coming back.

Maybe it's the complexity. Maybe it's the competition. Maybe it's the satisfaction of finally pulling off something you've been practicing for weeks.

Or maybe we've all just lost our minds.

Dota 2 isn't a game you simply finish. It's a journey with no final destination, where even after thousands of hours, there is still something new waiting to surprise you.

You don't always win. You don't always improve. Sometimes you don't even enjoy playing.

But when everything comes together, there is nothing quite like it.

**A beautiful disaster. An endless obsession. A game unlike any other.**

Would recommend. 10/10.
